Type checking for quantified collection predicates.\n\nuse crate::ast::{Expr, Quantifier};\nuse crate::spanned::Spanned;\n\nuse super::exprs::{View, type_of};\nuse super::types::{Ty, resolve};\nuse super::walk::Walker;\n\npub(super) fn type_collection_predicate(\n    w: &mut Walker<'_, '_>,\n    view: View<'_>,\n    collection: &Expr,\n    predicate: &Expr,\n    quantifier: Quantifier,\n) -> Ty {\n    let noun = match quantifier {\n        Quantifier::Any => \"any\",\n        Quantifier::All => \"all\",\n    };\n    let collection_ty = type_of(w, view, collection);\n    let element = match resolve(&collection_ty, &w.ctx.types) {\n        Ty::List(inner) => (*inner).clone(),\n        Ty::Unknown => Ty::Unknown,\n        other => {\n            w.err(\n                collection.span(),\n                format!(\"`{noun}` needs a List collection, found {other}\"),\n            );\n            Ty::Unknown\n        }\n    };\n    check_element_predicate(w, view, predicate, &element, noun);\n    Ty::Bool\n}\n\npub(super) fn check_element_predicate(\n    w: &mut Walker<'_, '_>,\n    view: View<'_>,\n    predicate: &Expr,\n    element: &Ty,\n    noun: &str,\n) {\n    let predicate_view = View {\n        vars: view.vars,\n        narrow: view.narrow,\n        accessor: Some(element),\n    };\n    let predicate_ty = type_of(w, predicate_view, predicate);\n    if !matches!(resolve(&predicate_ty, &w.ctx.types), Ty::Bool | Ty::Unknown) {\n        w.err(\n            predicate.span(),\n            format!(\"`{noun}` predicate must be Bool, found {predicate_ty}\"),\n        );\n    }\n}\n","numLines":57,"startLine":1,"totalLines":57}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"dc7220e8-dc1b-4ff9-aab9-e40fef6043f2","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/tom/Developer/ablative/stack/aion","sessionId":"5849e0d8-4802-4869-8e0f-9f7fd187e198","version":"2.1.222","gitBranch":"main","slug":"zazzy-whistling-stroustrup"}

crate::spanned::Spanned;\n\nuse super::collections::check_element_predicate;\nuse super::exprs::{View, field_access, type_of};\nuse super::outcomes::{Env, check_route};\nuse super::types::{Ty, assignable, resolve};\nuse super::walk::{Scope, Walker, insert_binding};\n\n/// Walk one pipe statement: type the head, thread it through every stage,\n/// then bind or route the final value.\npub(super) fn walk_pipe(\n    w: &mut Walker<'_, '_>,\n    scope: &mut Scope,\n    pipe: &PipeStmt,\n    env: &Env<'_>,\n) -> Option<Ty> {\n    let view = View {\n        vars: scope,\n        narrow: &[],\n        accessor: None,\n    };\n    let mut ty = type_of(w, view, &pipe.head);\n    for stage in &pipe.stages {\n        ty = pipe_stage(w, view, ty, stage);\n    }\n    match &pipe.end {\n        PipeEnd::Bind(bind) => {\n            insert_binding(w, scope, &bind.name, ty.clone(), bind.span);\n            Some(ty)\n        }\n        PipeEnd::Route(target) => {\n            let view = View {\n                vars: scope,\n                narrow: &[],\n                accessor: None,\n            };\n            check_route(w, view, target, env, Some(ty));\n            None\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn pipe_stage(w: &mut Walker<'_, '_>, view: View<'_>, incoming: Ty, stage: &PipeStage) -> Ty {\n    match stage {\n        PipeStage::Action { span, name } => {\n            let Some(callable) = w.ctx.callable(name).cloned() else {\n                w.err(\n                    *span,\n                    format!(\"no action or child named `{name}` is declared\"),\n                );\n                return Ty::Unknown;\n            };\n            if w.emit {\n                let kind = if w.ctx.actions.contains_key(name) {\n                    DeclarationKind::Action\n                } else {\n                    DeclarationKind::Child\n                };\n                w.ctx.semantic.reference(*span, kind, name);\n                w.ctx.semantic.ty(*span, &callable.returns.to_string());\n            }\n            // A stage exists to hand its value on, and an advisory action\n            // has no value to hand on when it fails (R5: it never faults the\n            // step, so the pipe would have to invent one).\n            if callable.advisory.is_some() {\n                w.err(\n                    *span,\n                    format!(\n                        \"advisory action `{name}` cannot be a pipe stage — an advisory \\\n                         failure never faults the step, so the stage would have no value \\\n                         to pass on; call it as a bare statement, or remove `advisory` \\\n                         from its declaration\"\n                    ),\n                );\n                return callable.returns;\n            }\n            if callable.params.len() != 1 {\n                w.err(\n                    *span,\n                    format!(\n                        \"`{name}` takes {} arguments and cannot be a pipe stage — a \\\n                         stage receives exactly one value\",\n                        callable.params.len()\n                    ),\n                );\n                return callable.returns;\n            }\n            let param = &callable.params[0];\n            if !assignable(&incoming, &param.ty, &w.ctx.types) {\n                w.err(\n                    *span,\n                    format!(\"pipe stage `{name}` expects {}, found {incoming}\", param.ty),\n                );\n            }\n            callable.returns\n        }\n        PipeStage::Field { span, name } => field_access(w, &incoming, None, name, *span),\n        PipeStage::Combinator(combinator) => combinator_stage(w, view, incoming, combinator),\n    }\n}\n\nfn combinator_stage(\n    w: &mut Walker<'_, '_>,\n    view: View<'_>,\n    incoming: Ty,\n    combinator: &CombinatorCall,\n) -> Ty {\n    let element = match resolve(&incoming, &w.ctx.types) {\n        Ty::List(inner) => (*inner).clone(),\n        Ty::Unknown => Ty::Unknown,\n        other => {\n            let noun = combinator_name(combinator.kind);\n            w.err(\n                combinator.span,\n                format!(\"`{noun}` needs a list to work over, found {other}\"),\n            );\n            Ty::Unknown\n        }\n    };\n    match combinator.kind {\n        CombinatorKind::Count => {\n            if combinator.arg.is_some() {\n                w.err(combinator.span, \"`count` takes no argument\");\n            }\n            Ty::Int\n        }\n        CombinatorKind::Filter => {\n            if let Some(field_ty) = accessor_field(w, combinator, &element) {\n                let resolved = resolve(&field_ty, &w.ctx.types);\n                if !matches!(resolved, Ty::Bool | Ty::Unknown)\n                    && let Some(Expr::Accessor { span, name }) = combinator.arg.as_ref()\n                {\n                    w.err(\n                        *span,\n                        format!(\n                            \"`filter` keeps items whose accessor is true — `.{name}` \\\n                             selects {field_ty}, not Bool\"\n                        ),\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n            incoming\n        }\n        CombinatorKind::Sort => {\n            accessor_field(w, combinator, &element);\n            incoming\n        }\n        CombinatorKind::Map => match accessor_field(w, combinator, &element) {\n            Some(field_ty) => Ty::List(Rc::new(field_ty)),\n            None => Ty::List(Rc::new(Ty::Unknown)),\n        },\n        CombinatorKind::Any | CombinatorKind::All => {\n            let noun = combinator_name(combinator.kind);\n            match combinator.arg.as_ref() {\n                Some(predicate) => check_element_predicate(w, view, predicate, &element, noun),\n                None => w.err(\n                    combinator.span,\n                    format!(\"`{noun}` needs a Bool predicate argument\"),\n                ),\n            }\n            Ty::Bool\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nconst fn combinator_name(kind: CombinatorKind) -> result.try({value} |> workflow.run |> awl_error.map_activity_error)\"\n        ));\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n    if let Some(&child) = emitter.children.get(name) {\n        let [param] = child.params.as_slice() else {\n            return Err(EmitError::new(\n                span,\n                format!(\n                    \"child `{name}` takes {} arguments — a pipe stage needs exactly one\",\n                    child.params.len()\n                ),\n            ));\n        };\n        let param_ty = type_ref_to_g(&param.ty);\n        let to_json = {to_json}({arg}))])\",\n            string_lit(&param.name)\n        );\n        let output_codec = emitter.child_output_codec_fn(&type_ref_to_g(&child.returns));\n        emitter.line(&format!(\n            \"use {fresh} <- result.try(workflow.spawn_and_wait({}, {CHILD_WITNESS}, {input}, \\\n             awlc.json_value(), {output_codec}(), awl_error.codec()) |> \\\n             awl_error.map_child_error)\",\n            string_lit(name)\n        ));\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n    Err(EmitError::new(\n        span,\n        format!(\"`{name}` names neither a declared action nor a child workflow\"),\n    ))\n}\n\n/// Wrap a rendered value in `Some(…)` when the slot is optional and the\n/// value is not.\npub(super) fn wrap_optional(\n    emitter: &Emitter<'_>,\n    rendered: String,\n    actual: &GType,\n    expected: &GType,\n) -> String {\n    if matches!(emitter.env.resolve(expected), GType::Option(_))\n        && !matches!(emitter.env.resolve(actual),  scope: &Scope,\n    stmts: &mut Vec<Stmt>,\n) -> Result<(Value, GType), LowerError> {\n    let (mut value, mut ty) = lower_expr(ctx, head, scope, stmts)?;\n    for stage in stages {\n        match stage {\n            PipeStage::Action { name, span } => {\n                if ctx.emitter.actions.contains_key(name.as_str()) {\n                    let call = Call {\n                        span: *span,\n                        name: name.clone(),\n                        name_span: *span,\n                        args: Vec::new(),\n                    };\n                    // Pipe stages carry no call-site config in the AST.\n                    let bound =\n                        activity_call(ctx, plan, &call, None, Some((value, ty)), scope, stmts)?;\n                    ty = ctx\n                        .emitter\n                        .actions\n                        .get(name.as_str())\n                        .map_or(GType::Unknown, |&(_, decl)| type_ref_to_g(&decl.returns));\n                    value = Value::Var(bound);\n                } else if ctx.emitter.children.contains_key(name.as_str()) {\n                    let (bound, returns) =\n                        pipe_child_stage(ctx, plan, name, *span, (value, ty), stmts)?;\n                    value = Value::Var(bound);\n                    ty = returns;\n                } else {\n format!(\"`{name}` names neither a declared action nor a child workflow\"),\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n            PipeStage::Field { name, span } => {\n Written order breaks no ties — it only\n  defines fall-through edges.\n- **Bindings** are single-assignment per scope; the `loop` threaded value\n  is the one sanctioned rebinding. Bindings flow forward along the graph;\n  the checker rejects reads of bindings not guaranteed on every path into\n  a step.\n- **Every dispatch, timer, signal, fork branch, and loop iteration is a\n  recorded event**; replay is deterministic because the language can\n  express nothing the log doesn't capture. Combinators replay as pure\n  recomputation.\n- **Exactly-once fan-out** (fork over collections) keeps the SDK `map`\n  semantics: per-item dedup keys, results ordered by input.\n\n## Mapping to the engine/SDK\n\n| engine/SDK primitive | AWL-2 |\n|---|---|\n| `workflow.run(activity)` | call statement in a step body |\n| `workflow.map` | `fork x in xs … join` |\n| `workflow.all` | named-branch `fork … join` |\n| sequential fold | **not expressible** — see below |\n| `child.spawn`/`await` | `child` declaration + call |\n| `child.spawn` (detached) | `spawn` |\n| `signal.receive` | `wait <signal>` |\n| timers / `with_timeout` | `sleep`; `timeout` on `wait`/actions |\n| retry/queue/node config | `retry`/`worker`/`node` on the action declaration |\n| terminal status | workflow `outcome … route success\\|failure` |\n| `continue_as_new` | deferred (unbounded loop gate, unchanged) |\n| `workflow.now/random` | deliberately absent (unchanged) |\n| codecs / schemas / start form | derived from `type`/`input`/`outcome` decls |\n\n**Sequential fold is not expressible in AWL-2**, and this table previously\nclaimed it was. The three mechanisms that would be needed are pairwise\nincompatible: `fork` iterates a collection but carries no accumulator\n(`ForkStmt` has `header`/`body`/`join` and no threaded value); `loop` threads\nexactly one value between iterations but has no collection binding; and\nindexing is literal-only — `Expr::Index` stores `index: u64` and its own doc\ncomment reads *\"Computed indices are unwritable\"*, so a loop counter can never\nbe used as a subscript. A numeric fold over a runtime-length collection\ntherefore has to be a worker action today. Tracked as issue #5, which proposes\n`sum` as a seventh `CombinatorKind` — a fixed type rule and no new binding\nform — ahead of a general `reduce`, which would need a two-argument lambda the\nlanguage has nowhere else.\n\n## Canonical formatting (printer contract)\n\n- Two-space indentation; declaration order as the grammar lists.\n- Type bodies: the 100-column single-line rule (unchanged).\n- One statement per line; a pipe chain longer than 100 columns breaks\n  before each `|>` with one extra indent.\n- Outcome clauses one per line; payload construction breaks after `route`","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"381a9364-3f7a-4ba5-a030-2a543501c61a","timestamp":"2026-08-06T06:42:09.475Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"## Semantics summary\n\n- **Scheduling**: a step is eligible when its `after` set is complete and\n  (if route-targeted) a route has fired; eligible steps with no mutual\n  dependency run concurrently. 9] = [\n    \"tools/tree-sitter-awl/queries/highlights.scm\",\n    \"tools/tree-sitter-awl/queries/indents.scm\",\n    \"tools/tree-sitter-awl/queries/folds.scm\",\n    \"editors/zed-awl/languages/awl/highlights.scm\",\n    \"editors/zed-awl/languages/awl/indents.scm\",\n    \"editors/zed-awl/languages/awl/outline.scm\",\n    \"editors/nvim-awl/queries/awl/highlights.scm\",\n    \"editors/nvim-awl/queries/awl/indents.scm\",\n    \"editors/nvim-awl/queries/awl/folds.scm\",\n];\n\n/// No editor colours less of the language than the authoritative query does.\n#[test]\nfn every_editor_covers_every_node_the_authoritative_query_colours() {\n    for (authority, copies) in QUERY_COVERAGE {\n        let expected = nodes_matched(&read(authority));\n        assert!(\n            expected.len() > 3,\n            \"{authority} yielded only {} node types, so the comparisons below would pass \\\n             vacuously — the extraction is broken, not the editors\",\n            expected.len()\n        );\n\n        for copy in copies {\n            let covered = nodes_matched(&read(copy));\n            let missing: Vec<&String> = expected.difference(&covered).collect();\n            assert!(\n                missing.is_empty(),\n                \"{copy} does not match these node types, which {authority} gives a capture to: \\\n                 {missing:?}\\nThe author sees them as plain text in that editor. Add a pattern \\\n                 for each, using that editor's own capture vocabulary — the capture NAME is free, \\\n                 the node coverage is not.\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Every node named in any query file is a node this grammar actually produces.\n///\n/// A pattern naming a node that no longer exists matches nothing and reports\n/// nothing; it is a colour that silently stopped applying. This is the reverse\n/// direction of the test above and catches a rename on the grammar side.\n#[test]\nfn no_query_names_a_node_the_grammar_does_not_produce() {\n    let node_types = read(\"tools/tree-sitter-awl/src/node-types.json\");\n    // Field names are legal in a pattern too (`name: (identifier)`), and they\n    // appear in node-types.json inside each node's \"fields\" object, so a single\n    // substring search over the file covers both without parsing it.\n    for query in ALL_QUERIES {\n        let unknown: Vec<String> = nodes_matched(&read(query))\n            .into_iter()\n            .filter(|node| !node_types.contains(&format!(\"\\\"{node}\\\"\")))\n            .collect();\n        assert!(\n            unknown.is_empty(),\n            \"{query} matches on node types absent from \\\n             tools/tree-sitter-awl/src/node-types.json: {unknown:?}\\nThose patterns match nothing \\\n             and colour nothing. Either the grammar renamed them and the query was not followed \\\n             through, or the names are typos.\"\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n/// The grammar sources the mirror publishes, in the order they are digested.\nconst PUBLISHED_GRAMMAR: [&str; 4] = [\n    \"tools/tree-sitter-awl/grammar.js\",\n    \"tools/tree-sitter-awl/src/grammar.json\",\n    \"tools/tree-sitter-awl/src/node-types.json\",\n    \"tools/tree-sitter-awl/src/parser.c\",\n];\n\n/// Digest of what a mirror commit must be carrying for the pin to be current.\n///\n/// Each file contributes its path and its length as well as its bytes, so a\n/// rename or a shift of content between files cannot leave the digest unchanged.\nfn published_grammar_digest() -> String {\n    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();\n    for relative in PUBLISHED_GRAMMAR {\n        let bytes = std::fs::read(repo_root().join(relative))\n            .unwrap_or_else(|error| unreachable!(\"{relative} is not readable: {error}\"));\n        hasher.update(relative.as_bytes());\n        hasher.update([0]);\n        hasher.update(u64::try_from(bytes.len()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX).to_le_bytes());\n        hasher.update(&bytes);\n    }\n    let mut hex = String::new();\n    for byte in hasher.finalize() {\n        use std::fmt::Write as _;\n        write!(hex, \"{byte:02x}\")\n            .unwrap_or_else(|error| unreachable!(\"writing hex into a String cannot fail: {error}\"));\n    }\n    hex\n}\n\n/// Read a `key = \"value\"` from the manifest's `[grammars.awl]` table, comments\n/// included.\n///\n/// Scoped to that table on purpose: `repository` is also a top-level key naming\n/// the aion repository itself, and reading the file as a flat list of lines\n/// would silently answer with that one — sending the publish-before-pin check\n/// at the wrong remote and passing.\nfn manifest_value(manifest: &str, key: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    manifest\n        .split_once(\"[grammars.awl]\")\n        .map_or(\"\", |(_, table)| table)\n        .lines()\n        // The table ends where the next one begins.\n        .take_while(|line| !line.trim_start().starts_with('['))\n        .map(str::trim_start)\n        .map(|line| line.trim_start_matches('#').trim_start())\n        .find_map(|line| {\n            let rest = line.strip_prefix(key)?.trim_start().strip_prefix('=')?;\n            let quoted = rest.trim().strip_prefix('\"')?;\n            quoted.split('\"').next().map(str::to_owned)\n        })\n}\n\n/// The Zed pin names a mirror commit carrying THIS grammar.\n///\n/// Zed does not build the grammar from this repository — it fetches\n/// `tools/tree-sitter-awl`'s published mirror at a fixed revision. So a grammar\n/// change here reaches Zed only after the mirror is pushed and the `rev` bumped,\n/// and until 2026-07-31 nothing said so out loud: the pin sat at `fa1afb22`\n/// while the grammar moved 436 commits underneath it.\n///\n/// The digest recorded beside the pin is what makes the staleness detectable\n/// offline. Change the grammar and this fires; the only way to quiet it is to\n/// do the thing that was missed — push the mirror, then record the new pair.\n#[test]\nfn the_zed_pin_names_a_mirror_commit_carrying_this_grammar() {\n    let manifest = read(\"editors/zed-awl/extension.toml\");\n    let Some(recorded) = manifest_value(&manifest, \"grammar-sha256\") else {\n        unreachable!(\n            \"editors/zed-awl/extension.toml carries no `# grammar-sha256 = \\\"…\\\"` line, so \\\n             nothing relates its `rev` to the grammar it is supposed to publish\"\n        )\n    };\n    let Some(rev) = manifest_value(&manifest, \"rev\") else {\n        unreachable!(\"editors/zed-awl/extension.toml carries no `rev`\")\n    };\n    assert_eq!(\n        rev.len(),\n        40,\n        \"the Zed `rev` must be a full 40-character sha, not `{rev}` — an abbreviated or symbolic \\\n         revision is not a fence\"\n    );\n\n    let actual = published_grammar_digest();\n    assert_eq!(\n        actual,\n        recorded,\n        \"\\nThe AWL grammar has changed since the Zed pin was recorded, so Zed is still fetching \\\n         the old parser and colouring the old language.\\n\\nTo clear this:\\n  1. cd \\\n         tools/tree-sitter-awl && tree-sitter generate && tree-sitter test\\n  2. sync \\\n         grammar.js, src/ and test/corpus/ into the tree-sitter-awl mirror checkout, commit and \\\n         push it\\n  3. verify anonymously: git ls-remote {} refs/heads/main\\n  4. set `rev` to \\\n         that sha and `# grammar-sha256` to {actual}\\n\\nDo not simply update the digest — that \\\n         records that the mirror was pushed when it was not.\\n\",\n        manifest_value(&manifest, \"repository\").unwrap_or_default()\n    );\n}\n\n/// The recorded pin is actually present on the public mirror.\n///\n/// This is the network half of the 2026-07-12 publish-before-pin ruling: a `rev`\n/// naming a sha that never reached the mirror resolves fine from an\n/// authenticated checkout and dies from the anonymous fetch that Zed performs.\n/// It cannot run offline, so it is gated at runtime rather than with\n/// `#[ignore]`, and it announces itself when it does not run.\n#[test]\nfn the_recorded_pin_is_present_on_the_public_mirror() {\n    if std::env::var(\"AION_VERIFY_MIRROR_PIN\").as_deref() != Ok(\"1\") {\n        println!(\n            \"SKIPPED: the publish-before-pin check reaches the network. Run it with \\\n             AION_VERIFY_MIRROR_PIN=1 before landing any change to editors/zed-awl/extension.toml.\"\n        );\n        return;\n    }\n\n    let manifest = read(\"editors/zed-awl/extension.toml\");\n    let Some(repository) = manifest_value(&manifest, \"repository\") else {\n        unreachable!(\"editors/zed-awl/extension.toml carries no `repository`\")\n    };\n    let Some(rev) = manifest_value(&manifest, \"rev\") else {\n        unreachable!(\"editors/zed-awl/extension.toml carries no `rev`\")\n    };\n\n    let output = std::process::Command::new(\"git\")\n        .args([\"ls-remote\", &repository, \"refs/heads/main\"])\n        .env(\"GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT\", \"0\")\n        .output()\n        .unwrap_or_else(|error| unreachable!(\"git ls-remote could not be run: {error}\"));\n    assert!(\n        output.status.success(),\n        \"anonymous `git ls-remote {repository}` failed, which is exactly what a Zed user's \\\n         grammar fetch does:\\n{}\",\n        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)\n    );\n\n    let listing = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n    let head = listing.split_whitespace().next().unwrap_or_default();\n    assert_eq!(\n        head, rev,\n        \"the public mirror's main is at {head}, but editors/zed-awl/extension.toml pins {rev}. \\\n         Either the pinned commit was never pushed — the failure this check exists for — or the \\\n         mirror has moved ahead and the pin is stale.\"\n    );\n}\n","numLines":313,"startLine":1,"totalLines":313}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"fbdb96e4-a4f0-4ce3-9f51-a5a18fa12a28","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/tom/Developer/ablative/stack/aion","sessionId":"5849e0d8-4802-4869-8e0f-9f7fd187e198","version":"2.1.222","gitBranch":"main","slug":"zazzy-whistling-stroustrup"}

A plain statement opener is a\n/// cosmetic loss; a tinted binding is the editor lying about the author's code.\nconst COLOURED_POSITIONAL_WORDS: [&str; 1] = [\"in\"];\n\n/// Reserved words the grammar colours through a MORE specific node than\n/// `keyword`, paired with the rule that must still cover them.\n///\n/// `true` and `false` are `Keyword` variants here, but the grammar gives them\n/// `boolean: _ => choice('true','false')` so an editor can render them as\n/// constants rather than as syntax. found, so every assertion below \\\n         would pass vacuously\",\n        grammar.len()\n    );\n\n    let missing: Vec<&str> = Keyword::ALL\n        .iter()\n        .map(|keyword| keyword.as_word())\n        .filter(|word| !grammar.iter().any(|listed| listed == word))\n        .filter(|word| {\n            !SPECIFICALLY_TYPED_WORDS\n                .iter()\n                .any(|(typed, _)| typed == word)\n        })\n        .collect();\n    assert!(\n        missing.is_empty(),\n        \"these words are reserved by the AWL lexer but absent from \\\n         tools/tree-sitter-awl/grammar.js, so they render as ordinary identifiers in the ops \\\n         console and in every editor: {missing:?}\\nAdd them to `const keywords`, re-run \\\n {\n    let reserved: Vec<&str> = Keyword::ALL\n        .iter()\n        .map(|keyword| keyword.as_word())\n        .collect();\n    let unexplained: Vec<String> = grammar_keywords()\n        .into_iter()\n        .filter(|word| !reserved.contains(&word.as_str()))\n        .filter(|word| !COLOURED_POSITIONAL_WORDS.contains(&word.as_str()))\n        .collect();\n    assert!(\n        unexplained.is_empty(),\n        \"tools/tree-sitter-awl/grammar.js colours these words, but the AWL lexer neither reserves \\\n         them nor lists them as a deliberate positional-word exception: which is the opposite of what it\n/// is for.\n#[test]\nfn the_specifically_typed_words_are_still_covered() {\n    for (word, rule) in SPECIFICALLY_TYPED_WORDS {\n        let Some((_, rest)) = GRAMMAR.split_once(&format!(\"{rule}:\")) else {\n            unreachable!(\n                \"the grammar has no `{rule}:` rule, so `{word}` is exempted from the \\\n                 reserved-word gate while nothing in the grammar covers it\"\n            )\n        };\n        let body = &rest[..rest.len().min(200)];\n        assert!(\n            body.contains(&format!(\"'{word}'\")),\n {\n        assert!(\n            POSITIONAL_WORDS.contains(&word),\n            \"`{word}` is listed as a coloured positional word but is not one of AWL's positional \\\n             words, so the Pins on the vocabulary inventories every consumer outside the lexer reads.\n2\t\n3\tuse super::tokens::{\n4\t    ANSWER_WORD, IN_WORD, Keyword, POSITIONAL_WORDS, QUERY_WORD, RUN_WORD, SEND_WORD, TO_WORD,\n5\t};\n6\t\n7\t/// The window of `tokens.rs` holding `as_word`'s match arms: one arm per\n8\t/// keyword, and the only place in the file where the arms can be counted\n9\t/// without writing the count down a second time.\n10\tfn as_word_arm_count() -> usize {\n11\t    let source = include_str!(\"tokens.rs\");\n12\t    let after = source\n13\t        .split_once(\"pub const fn as_word\")\n14\t        .map(|(_, rest)| rest)\n15\t        .unwrap_or_default();\n16\t    let body = after\n17\t        .split_once(\"pub fn from_word\")\n18\t        .map(|(body, _)| body)\n19\t        .unwrap_or_default();\n20\t    body.matches(\"Self::\").count()\n21\t}\n22\t\n23\t/// [`Keyword::ALL`] is the whole language, not most of it.\n24\t///\n25\t/// Rust cannot enumerate an enum's variants, so `ALL` is written by hand and a\n26\t/// hand-written list of 57 things silently loses an entry. The count is\n27\t/// therefore DERIVED from `as_word`'s own source rather than restated: adding a\n28\t/// variant adds an arm there (the compiler forces it — the match is\n29\t/// exhaustive) and this test fails until `ALL` is extended too.\n30\t///\n31\t/// Assert the invariant, not the enumeration: comparing against a literal 57\n32\t/// would only pin what was true the day it was typed.\n33\t#[test]\n34\tfn keyword_inventory_covers_every_variant() {\n35\t    let arms = as_word_arm_count();\n36\t    assert!(\n37\t        arms > 50,\n38\t        \"the control failed: the arm count is derived by reading this crate's own source, and a \\\n39\t         parse that found {arms} arms is not reading `as_word` at all — the comparison below \\\n40\t         would pass vacuously\"\n41\t    );\n42\t    assert_eq!(\n43\t        Keyword::ALL.len(),\n44\t        arms,\n45\t        \"`Keyword::ALL` lists {} of the language's {arms} reserved words. A keyword missing from \\\n46\t         it does not fail to compile — it goes quietly absent from every consumer that reads the \\\n47\t         vocabulary, starting with the language server's completions.\",\n48\t        Keyword::ALL.len()\n49\t    );\n50\t}\n51\t\n52\t/// Every entry in the inventory is a distinct, real word.\n53\t///\n54\t/// A duplicated entry would keep the count right while losing a keyword, which\n55\t/// is exactly the failure the count is meant to catch.\n56\t#[test]\n57\tfn every_keyword_in_the_inventory_round_trips_and_is_distinct() {\n58\t    let mut seen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();\n59\t    for keyword in Keyword::ALL {\n60\t        let word = keyword.as_word();\n61\t        assert_eq!(\n62\t            Keyword::from_word(word),\n63\t            Some(keyword),\n64\t            \"`{word}` must lex back to the keyword it was written from\"\n65\t        );\n66\t        assert!(\n67\t            seen.insert(word),\n68\t            \"`{word}` appears twice in `Keyword::ALL`, which keeps the count right while losing a \\\n69\t             keyword\"\n70\t        );\n71\t    }\n72\t    assert_eq!(seen.len(), Keyword::ALL.len());\n73\t}\n74\t\n75\t/// The positional words are NOT reserved, and must stay that way.\n76\t///\n77\t/// This is the load-bearing property of that list, not an incidental one: the\n78\t/// corpus carries `action send(to: String, …)`, `step run` and `wait decision\n79\t/// -> answer`. If one of these ever became a keyword, those documents would\n80\t/// stop parsing — so the inventory that names them for outside consumers also\n81\t/// pins that naming them did not reserve them.\n82\t#[test]\n83\tfn the_positional_words_are_named_without_being_reserved() {\n84\t    for word in POSITIONAL_WORDS {\n85\t        assert_eq!(\n86\t            Keyword::from_word(word),\n87\t            None,\n88\t            \"`{word}` is read positionally and must never lex as a keyword — reserving it breaks \\\n89\t             documents that exist today\"\n90\t        );\n91\t    }\n92\t    assert_eq!(\n93\t        POSITIONAL_WORDS,\n94\t        [\n95\t            SEND_WORD,\n96\t            TO_WORD,\n97\t            QUERY_WORD,\n98\t            ANSWER_WORD,\n99\t            RUN_WORD,\n100\t            IN_WORD\n101\t        ],\n102\t        \"the inventory must hold every named positional word, or a consumer reading it offers \\\n103\t         fewer words than the parser accepts\"\n104\t    );\n105\t}\n106\t"}]},"uuid":"23de5b9b-b9a4-44a8-a79f-e67c4d2761a7","timestamp":"2026-08-06T06:43:06.975Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/tom/Developer/ablative/stack/aion/crates/aion-awl/src/lexer/tokens_tests.rs","content":"//! Pins on the vocabulary inventories every consumer outside the lexer reads.\n\nuse super::tokens::{\n    ANSWER_WORD, IN_WORD, Keyword, POSITIONAL_WORDS, QUERY_WORD, RUN_WORD, SEND_WORD, TO_WORD,\n};\n\n/// The window of `tokens.rs` holding `as_word`'s match arms: one arm per\n/// keyword, and the only place in the file where the arms can be counted\n/// without writing the count down a second time.\nfn as_word_arm_count() -> usize {\n    let source = include_str!(\"tokens.rs\");\n    let after = source\n        .split_once(\"pub const fn as_word\")\n        .map(|(_, rest)| rest)\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    let body = after\n        .split_once(\"pub fn from_word\")\n        .map(|(body, _)| body)\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    body.matches(\"Self::\").count()\n}\n\n/// [`Keyword::ALL`] is the whole language, not most of it.\n///\n/// Rust cannot enumerate an enum's variants, so `ALL` is written by hand and a\n/// hand-written list of 57 things silently loses an entry. The count is\n/// therefore DERIVED from `as_word`'s own source rather than restated: adding a\n/// variant adds an arm there (the compiler forces it — the match is\n/// exhaustive) and this test fails until `ALL` is extended too.\n///\n/// Assert the invariant, not the enumeration: comparing against a literal 57\n/// would only pin what was true the day it was typed.\n#[test]\nfn keyword_inventory_covers_every_variant() {\n    let arms = as_word_arm_count();\n    assert!(\n        arms > 50,\n        \"the control failed: the arm count is derived by reading this crate's own source, and a \\\n         parse that found {arms} arms is not reading `as_word` at all — the comparison below \\\n         would pass vacuously\"\n    );\n    assert_eq!(\n        Keyword::ALL.len(),\n        arms,\n        \"`Keyword::ALL` lists {} of the language's {arms} reserved words. A keyword missing from \\\n         it does not fail to compile — it goes quietly absent from every consumer that reads the \\\n         vocabulary, starting with the language server's completions.\",\n        Keyword::ALL.len()\n    );\n}\n\n/// Every entry in the inventory is a distinct, real word.\n///\n/// A duplicated entry would keep the count right while losing a keyword, which\n/// is exactly the failure the count is meant to catch.\n#[test]\nfn every_keyword_in_the_inventory_round_trips_and_is_distinct() {\n    let mut seen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();\n    for keyword in Keyword::ALL {\n        let word = keyword.as_word();\n        assert_eq!(\n            Keyword::from_word(word),\n            Some(keyword),\n            \"`{word}` must lex back to the keyword it was written from\"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            seen.insert(word),\n            \"`{word}` appears twice in `Keyword::ALL`, which keeps the count right while losing a \\\n             keyword\"\n        );\n    }\n    assert_eq!(seen.len(), Keyword::ALL.len());\n}\n\n/// The positional words are NOT reserved, and must stay that way.\n///\n/// This is the load-bearing property of that list, not an incidental one: the\n/// corpus carries `action send(to: String, …)`, `step run` and `wait decision\n/// -> answer`. If one of these ever became a keyword, those documents would\n/// stop parsing — so the inventory that names them for outside consumers also\n/// pins that naming them did not reserve them.\n#[test]\nfn the_positional_words_are_named_without_being_reserved() {\n    for word in POSITIONAL_WORDS {\n        assert_eq!(\n            Keyword::from_word(word),\n            None,\n            \"`{word}` is read positionally and must never lex as a keyword — reserving it breaks \\\n             documents that exist today\"\n        );\n    }\n    assert_eq!(\n        POSITIONAL_WORDS,\n        [\n            SEND_WORD,\n            TO_WORD,\n            QUERY_WORD,\n            ANSWER_WORD,\n            RUN_WORD,\n            IN_WORD\n        ],\n        \"the inventory must hold every named positional word, or a consumer reading it offers \\\n         fewer words than the parser accepts\"\n    );\n}\n","numLines":106,"startLine":1,"totalLines":106}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"1b7c117f-dd01-46b0-ad99-667d03f2d3a5","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/tom/Developer/ablative/stack/aion","sessionId":"5849e0d8-4802-4869-8e0f-9f7fd187e198","version":"2.1.222","gitBranch":"main","slug":"zazzy-whistling-stroustrup"}

Static lowering/bundle skew guard: every `(module, function, arity)` the\n//! MIR lowering may mint (`RuntimeFn::import_surface`) must be exported by a\n//! module shipped in the embedded SDK closure.\n//!\n//! This is the guard the `map_settled` incident demanded: the lowering grew a\n//! `RuntimeFn` row (`aion@workflow:map_settled/2`) while the committed\n//! closure predated the SDK function, so tolerant single-activity distribute\n//! archives crashed a running VM with `undef` — a skew no compile step could\n//! see. With this test, a runtime row the closure does not export fails CI\n//! the moment it is introduced.\n\nuse std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};\n\nuse aion_awl::mir::RuntimeFn;\nuse aion_awl_package::sdk_closure_modules;\nuse beamr::atom::AtomTable;\nuse beamr::loader::load_beam_chunks;\n\ntype TestResult = Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>;\n\n/// Modules the Erlang runtime itself provides. `RuntimeFn::IntAdd` is the one\n/// BIF-position row (`erlang:'+'/2`); beamr resolves it natively, so no\n/// bundle module can or should export it.\nconst VM_PROVIDED_MODULES: &[&str] = &[\"erlang\"];\n\n/// Module name → exported `(function, arity)` set.\ntype ExportMap = BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<(String, u32)>>;\n\n/// The export map of the embedded closure, read through the same beamr\n/// chunk loader the engine uses.\nfn closure_exports() -> Result<ExportMap, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let atoms = AtomTable::with_common_atoms();\n    let mut exports = BTreeMap::new();\n    for (name, bytes) in sdk_closure_modules() {\n        let parsed = load_beam_chunks(bytes, &atoms)?;\n        let mut set = BTreeSet::new();\n        for export in &parsed.exports {\n            let Some(function) = atoms.resolve(export.function) else {\n                return Err(format!(\n                    \"module `{name}` has an unresolvable export atom: {:?}\",\n                    export.function\n                )\n                .into());\n            };\n            set.insert((function.to_owned(), u32::from(export.arity)));\n        }\n        exports.insert(name.to_owned(), set);\n    }\n    Ok(exports)\n}\n\n/// Every runtime signature the lowering may mint is exported by a shipped\n/// closure module (VM-provided modules excepted).\n#[test]\nfn every_runtime_fn_signature_is_exported_by_the_closure() -> TestResult {\n    let exports = closure_exports()?;\n    let surface = RuntimeFn::import_surface();\n    // Vacuous-pass guards: the surface and the closure must both be\n    // non-trivial, and the incident row itself must be present.\n    assert!(surface.len() > 50, \"runtime surface shrank suspiciously\");\n    assert!(!exports.is_empty(), \"closure export map is empty\");\n    assert!(\n        surface.iter().any(|(module, function, arity)| {\n            *module == \"aion@workflow\" && function == \"map_settled\" && *arity == 2\n        }),\n        \"the surface no longer carries aion@workflow:map_settled/2 — update this guard's anchors\"\n    );\n\n    let mut missing = Vec::new();\n    for (module, function, arity) in surface {\n        if VM_PROVIDED_MODULES.contains(&module) {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let exported = exports\n            .get(module)\n            .is_some_and(|set| set.contains(&(function.clone(), arity)));\n        if !exported {\n            missing.push(format!(\"{module}:{function}/{arity}\"));\n        }\n    }\n    assert!(\n        missing.is_empty(),\n        \"runtime rows the embedded SDK closure does not export (each would be an `undef` crash \\\n         in a deployed direct archive): {missing:?}\"\n    );\n    Ok(())\n}\n","numLines":88,"startLine":1,"totalLines":88}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"a310a960-bbad-4ca0-9392-baddbcf5f883","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/tom/Developer/ablative/stack/aion","sessionId":"5849e0d8-4802-4869-8e0f-9f7fd187e198","version":"2.1.222","gitBranch":"main","slug":"zazzy-whistling-stroustrup"}

The bytes live in [`super::bundle_data`], a committed file\n//! generated by `scripts/regen-awl-sdk-closure.sh` (a dev-time step that\n//! requires a local `gleam`; no build.rs or product path calls it).\n\nuse super::bundle_data;\n\n/// Returns the `aion_flow` SDK version the embedded closure was built from.\n#[must_use]\npub fn sdk_closure_version() -> &'static str {\n    bundle_data::SDK_CLOSURE_VERSION\n}\n\n/// Iterates the embedded closure as `(logical module name, .beam bytes)`\n/// pairs, sorted by module name.\npub fn sdk_closure_modules() -> impl Iterator<Item = (&'static str, &'static [u8])> {\n    bundle_data::MODULES\n        .iter()\n        .map(|(name, bytes)| (*name, *bytes))\n}\n\n/// Returns true when the closure ships a module with this logical name.\npub(crate) fn contains(name: &str) -> bool {\n    bundle_data::MODULES\n        .binary_search_by(|(module, _)| (*module).cmp(name))\n        .is_ok()\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::{contains, sdk_closure_modules, sdk_closure_version};","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"d469a343-b790-4f57-a2e6-6c7f5925c7f6","timestamp":"2026-08-06T06:43:34.602Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"//! The three ratified language rulings (Tom, 2026-07-11), pinned beyond the\n//! corpus fixtures' substring/line contract:\n//!\n//! R1. Loop exhaustion must be explicitly named — a loop-carrying step with\n//!     zero outcome clauses is a check error anchored at the loop.\n//! R2. `?` is illegal in list-element position — `[T?]` is refused in every\n//!     type position; `[T]?` (the whole list absent) stays legal.\n//! R3. `route` is illegal inside a `loop` body — statement and pipe-chain\n//!     terminator alike; the refusal is the checker's (the emitter keeps a\n//!     defensive backstop for unchecked documents).\n\nuse std::error::Error;\n\nuse aion_awl::{CheckError, check, parse};\n\ntype TestResult = Result<(), Box<dyn Error>>;\n\nfn check_source(source: &str) -> Result<Vec<CheckError>, Box<dyn Error>> {\n    let document = parse(source).map_err(|error| {\n        format!(\n            \"failed to parse: {} at line {}, column {}\",\n            error.message, error.span.line, error.span.column\n        )\n    })?;\n    Ok(check(&document))\n}\n\nfn line_of(source: &str, needle: &str) -> Result<usize, Box<dyn Error>> {\n    let start = source\n        .find(needle)\n        .ok_or_else(|| format!(\"missing needle {needle:?}\"))?;\n    Ok(source[..start].matches('\\n').count() + 1)\n}\n\nfn find_error<'e>(\n    errors: &'e [CheckError],\n    substring: &str,\n    line: usize,\n) -> Result<&'e CheckError, Box<dyn Error>> {\n    errors\n        .iter()\n        .find(|error| error.message.contains(substring) && error.span.line == line)\n        .ok_or_else(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"no diagnostic contains {substring:?} at line {line}; got {:#?}\",\n                errors\n                    .iter()\n                    .map(|error| format!(\"line {}: {}\", error.span.line, error.message))\n                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            )\n            .into()\n        })\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n// R1 — loop exhaustion must be explicitly named\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// A loop inside a collection-fork branch still puts the exhaustion duty on\n/// the owning step: the scan looks through fork bodies.\n#[test]\nfn loop_inside_a_fork_branch_still_requires_outcome_clauses() -> TestResult {\n    let source = \"\\\n//! Each branch polls to completion; the step never names exhaustion.\nworkflow fan_poll\n  input job_ids: [String]\n  outcome done: type Tally, route success\n\ntype Poll  { state: String, done: Bool }\ntype Tally { polled: Int }","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"a95da95c-54f7-4402-a930-9e9dbf63825b","timestamp":"2026-08-06T06:47:17.809Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"//! The three are pairwise incompatible.\n\n**`AWL-2-SPEC.md` claimed the opposite** — a mapping row reading *\"sequential\nfold | `fork … sequential` or `loop`\"* — a documented capability that does not\nexist, and one that would have caused this issue to be wrongly closed as\nalready-supported by anyone triaging against the spec. **Corrected in this\ncommit**, with the reason stated inline.\n\n⇒ `sum` first: a seventh variant, a fixed type rule, no new binding form, and\ncombinators already replay as pure recomputation. A general `reduce` needs a\ntwo-argument lambda the language has nowhere else. Landing it must bump\n`Keyword::ALL`'s `[Self; 57]` in the same change — the length assertion is what\nforces those two places to agree.\n\n## #1 — the contract is documented and violated\n\n`nif_context.rs:118` takes `history.last()`, and the context is rebuilt fresh\non every NIF call, so `now()` is a function of history length at call time, not\nof replay position. `workflows.md:65-66` promises the opposite: *\"it returns\nthe recorded event timestamp, identical on every replay.\"*\n\nSmall correction to the issue: the value is not fixed at `T_wake` forever, it\nis the tail at each call — constant through the replay window, then advancing\nagain. That does not weaken the claim.\n\n**One husk and one pin defending the defect.**\n`replay_sequence_matches_recorded_history_and_seeded_positions` builds both\ncontexts over the *same* history vector, so the two `now` values are equal by\nconstruction and the assertion cannot fail either way — its model of \"replay\"\nis the one case the defect does not affect. The language-design call\n\n### Recommendation: **`sum` as a seventh `CombinatorKind`, zero-argument, pipe-stage only.** Not a general fold.\n\n```awl\nitems |> map(.amount) |> sum -> total\n```\n\nType rule (total, no cases left open):\n\n| incoming | result |\n|---|---|\n| `[Int]` | `Int` |\n| `[Float]` | `Float` |\n| anything else | **check error** |\n\nEmpty list → `0` / `0.0`. This is **not an assumed default**: it is the identity element of addition and it is what `gleam@int:sum/1` computes (`sum_loop(numbers, 0)`, verified in the stdlib source). There is no configurable value here to invent.\n\n### Why not a general fold/reduce — the honest case against, and why it still loses\n\nThe general form is the *principled* answer: `sum` is one instance, and a language that only ships instances accretes `min`, `max`, `average`, `product` one keyword at a time. CLAUDE.md's \"no shortcuts\" instinct points at `reduce`.\n\nIt loses on four counts, all of them structural rather than aesthetic:\n\n1. **A fold needs three things AWL deliberately does not have.** A two-argument lambda (the language has *no* user functions — spec line 328: *\"no user functions, no arithmetic beyond comparison and string `+`\"*); arithmetic operators (refused at `checker/operators.rs:68`); and an accumulator binding form in expression position. Every combinator argument today is a `.field` accessor or a literal (`accessor_field`, `checker/stages.rs:187-206`). `reduce(acc, item -> acc + item.amount)` is not a seventh combinator — it is a second expression language.\n\n2. **It would drag arithmetic in through the back door.** Once `+` works inside a fold body it must work everywhere or the language has two arithmetics. Introducing arithmetic to AWL is a decision with its own overflow, division-by-zero, Int/Float-coercion and determinism surface. That is a design conversation, not a bug fix.\n\n3. **The direct backend cost is an order of magnitude apart.** `sum` = two `RuntimeFn` rows + one `CallRt` (finding 1 above). `reduce` = a new MIR `Stmt::Add` (or a general `BinArith`), a new `gc_bif2` burst, a `verify` capability arm, a printer arm, and — because the fold body is user code — a *capturing* lifted closure, where today's combinator closures are all capture-free (`MakeClosure { captures: Vec::new() }`, `mir/lower/pipes.rs:227,286`).\n\n4. **`sum` does not paint us into a corner, which is the real cost you were weighing.** It establishes the *reducer slot*: an argument-less combinator whose type rule maps `[T] → T'`. `min`, `max`, `average`, `product` are then each ~15 lines in exactly the same five places, with zero re-design and zero migration — `gleam@int:product/1` and `gleam@float:product/1` are already exported by the closure too (verified). The thing we would have to widen \"next month\" is a *table*, not a *form*. A narrow `sum` is only a real cost when the narrow thing and the general thing have different shapes; here the narrow thing is a row in the general thing's table.\n\n### Two sub-decisions, stated so they are not silently made\n\n- **`sum` takes no argument.** Not `sum(.amount)`. `map(.amount) |> sum` already expresses it, exactly as `count` composes with `filter`. Adding an optional accessor would put one truth (how you project before reducing) in two places, and duplicate `map`'s field-type check. Refuse the argument explicitly.\n- **The type gate lives in the CHECKER, not only in the backends.** `docs/design/fanout-observability/awl-pipes-spec.md:13` records the existing defect that `sort`'s key-comparability gate lives *only* in the emitter, so *\"a check-clean document can reach lowering with a non-comparable sort key.\"* `sum` must not repeat that: `aion awl check` refuses a non-numeric sum, and both backends keep matching defensive refusals for unchecked documents.\n\n---\n\n## 3. What follows are the updates the *landing* requires, plus one genuinely stale doc.\n\n### `docs/design/aion-authoring/awl/AWL-2-SPEC.md`\n\n| Line | Current | Replacement |\n|---|---|---|\n| 58 | `executed in the workflow VM (\\`filter\\`, \\`map\\`, \\`sort\\`, \\`count\\`, \\`any\\`, \\`all\\`);` | `executed in the workflow VM (\\`filter\\`, \\`map\\`, \\`sort\\`, \\`count\\`, \\`sum\\`, \\`any\\`, \\`all\\`);` |\n| 311 | `` `count`, `any(pred)`, `all(pred)`, plus the predicates `is empty`, `` | `` `count`, `sum`, `any(pred)`, `all(pred)`, plus the predicates `is empty`, `` |\n| 464 | `` \\| combinators/predicates \\| `filter` `map` `sort` `count` `any` `all` `is` `empty` `present` `absent` \\| `` | `` \\| combinators/predicates \\| `filter` `map` `sort` `count` `sum` `any` `all` `is` `empty` `present` `absent` \\| `` |\n| 500 | `\\| sequential fold \\| **not expressible** — see below \\|` | `` \\| numeric fold over a collection \\| `xs \\|> sum` (Int/Float; `map` first to project) \\| ``<br>`\\| general sequential fold \\| **not expressible** — see below \\|` |\n| 511-521 | The whole paragraph beginning *\"**Sequential fold is not expressible in AWL-2**, and this table previously claimed it was.\"* | Replace with:<br><br>**A numeric fold is expressible; a general one is not.** `xs \\|> sum` reduces a `[Int]` to an `Int` and a `[Float]` to a `Float` (empty list → the additive identity), and composes with `map` for the field case: `items \\|> map(.amount) \\|> sum`. It is a combinator, so it replays as pure recomputation like the other six.<br><br>A **general** fold remains out of reach, and the three mechanisms that would supply one are pairwise incompatible: `fork` iterates a collection but carries no accumulator (`ForkStmt` has `header`/`body`/`join` and no threaded value); `loop` threads exactly one value between iterations but has no collection binding; and indexing is literal-only — `Expr::Index` stores `index: u64` and its own doc comment reads *\"Computed indices are unwritable\"*, so a loop counter can never be used as a subscript. Beyond that, AWL has no arithmetic at all (`+` joins strings; `checker/operators.rs` refuses numeric operands) and no user functions, so a `reduce(acc, item -> …)` body has nowhere to be written. A non-numeric fold is still a worker action. An earlier revision of this table claimed `fork … sequential` or `loop` supplied a sequential fold; it did not, and that claim was withdrawn on 2026-08-06. |\n| 649 | `no arithmetic beyond comparisons and string \\`+\\`;
